lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Checkout Walkthrough: Breakfast Feedback to the Manager
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Review the stay's breakfasts with the manager, give balanced feedback, and agree on conditions for returning.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are checking out of apartment 7B, and the AI is Gonzalo, the apart-hotel manager: review the stay's breakfasts, give balanced feedback, and set conditions for returning with volvería siempre que…, sería ideal que… and the conditional.
lessons.sourceGrammarFocusEnglish: Conditional; subjunctive in conditions (volvería siempre que haya pan sin gluten; sería ideal que…)

sourceWordsEnglish.en: Overall, we loved the breakfast, especially the seasonal fruit.
The only thing I'd improve is the variety of celiac-safe options.
We'd come back as long as there's gluten-free bread every day.
It would be ideal if you restocked the fruit more often in the morning.
If you gave us 7B again, we'd gladly book.
We'd come back in March provided the rate is similar.
Gonzalo, I'll gladly leave you a good review on the platform.
Kids, what did you like most about the breakfast?

sourcePassageEnglish: On Sunday at 10, Laura hands in the key to apartment 7B at the front desk of the apart-hotel in Pocitos.
Gonzalo, the manager, asks her how the stay went and what it would take for the family to book again.
Laura: Overall, we loved the breakfast, especially the seasonal fruit.
Laura: Kids, what did you like most about the breakfast?
Sofía says the homemade granola was the strong point, because she ate it every morning with yogurt.
Gonzalo asks whether anyone in the family has an allergy or a dietary restriction.
Laura explains that Tomás is celiac and can only eat products that are safe for celiacs.
Laura: The only thing I'd improve is the variety of celiac-safe options.
She says the gluten-free selection was good on Monday, but on Wednesday there were only crackers left.
Laura: We'd come back as long as there's gluten-free bread every day.
Another weak point was the butter, because it came in a shared tub and Tomás couldn't use it without a risk of cross-contamination.
Laura: It would be ideal if the butter came in individual portions.
Gonzalo writes down the feedback and says he is going to talk to the kitchen this week.
Gonzalo: For your next visit, we have a special offer with a 15% discount on stays of 5 nights or more.
Laura: We'd come back in March provided the rate is similar.
Laura: If you gave us 7B again, we'd gladly book.
Gonzalo asks what score she would give the breakfast, and Laura answers that she would give it a 9 out of 10.
Laura: Gonzalo, I'll gladly leave you a good review on the platform.

sourceVerbsEnglish.exampleEnglish: We're coming back in March with the kids.
The kitchen is improving the gluten-free selection this week.
I'll gladly leave you a good review.
Gonzalo asks how the stay went.

sourceGrammarExamplesEnglish: I'd come back as long as there's gluten-free bread at breakfast.
It would be ideal if the butter came in individual portions.
lessons.titleFrenchCourseEnglish: Faire un bilan du petit-déjeuner au départ
lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Donner un retour équilibré sur le séjour et préciser ce qu’il faudrait confirmer avant une prochaine réservation.
lessons.focusEnglish: Conditional and conditions: I would return if the room and dietary information were confirmed in writing.
lessons.focusFrench: Conditionnel et conditions : je reviendrais si la chambre et les renseignements alimentaires étaient confirmés par écrit.
lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: A dietary label or extra option does not establish suitability for coeliac disease. The family asks for ingredient/preparation details and makes no promise to rebook.

passage.titleFrench: Faire un bilan du petit-déjeuner au départ
english: At checkout in a Québec City aparthotel, Laura returns the key to apartment seven B.
The manager, Gabriel, asks how the family liked the breakfasts.
Laura says that the seasonal fruit was a strong point.
Her daughter says she liked the granola.
Laura explains that her son has coeliac disease and needs reliable ingredient and preparation information.
She does not describe any buffet item as safe based on its label alone.
She says the information was clear on one morning but hard to find on another.
Laura asks whether the staff can explain how the granola and bread are prepared.
Gabriel says he will ask the kitchen and send a factual reply.
Laura adds that the fruit could have been replenished earlier.
Gabriel writes down both the compliment and the concern.
He asks whether the family might return.
Laura says she would consider it if the room, rate and dietary details were confirmed in writing.
She does not accept an offer before seeing its terms.
Gabriel says he can send a quote for a later stay.
Laura says she can leave a balanced review after checking out.
She thanks him for listening and asks when the kitchen reply might arrive.
The family leaves without treating the future booking as settled.
french: Au départ d’un appart-hôtel à Québec, Laura rend la clé de l’appartement sept B.
Le responsable, Gabriel, demande comment la famille a trouvé les petits-déjeuners.
Laura dit que les fruits de saison étaient un point fort.
Sa fille dit qu’elle a aimé le granola.
Laura explique que son fils a la maladie cœliaque et qu’il a besoin de renseignements fiables sur les ingrédients et la préparation.
Elle ne décrit aucun produit du buffet comme sûr sur la seule base de son étiquette.
Elle dit que les renseignements étaient clairs un matin, mais difficiles à trouver un autre.
Laura demande si le personnel peut expliquer comment le granola et le pain sont préparés.
Gabriel dit qu’il interrogera la cuisine et enverra une réponse factuelle.
Laura ajoute que les fruits auraient pu être réapprovisionnés plus tôt.
Gabriel note à la fois le compliment et la préoccupation.
Il demande si la famille envisage de revenir.
Laura dit qu’elle l’envisagerait si la chambre, le tarif et les renseignements alimentaires étaient confirmés par écrit.
Elle n’accepte aucune offre avant d’en voir les conditions.
Gabriel dit qu’il peut envoyer un devis pour un prochain séjour.
Laura dit qu’elle peut laisser un avis équilibré après son départ.
Elle le remercie de l’avoir écoutée et demande quand la réponse de la cuisine pourrait arriver.
La famille part sans considérer la prochaine réservation comme conclue.

lessons.sourceTitleEnglish: Capstone: A Group Breakfast in Puebla Goes Sideways
lessons.sourceObjectiveEnglish: Lead a group through a hard breakfast morning: teach, solve, refuse, report, message and close it out in Spanish.
lessons.sourceSpeakingEnglish: You are leading five relatives through a Puebla breakfast, and the AI is Emilio, server Brenda, the host and the manager: coach Emilio's order, check tía Rosa's allergens, order for all, text the host and give checkout feedback, using commands, conditionals and the subjunctive.

sourceWordsEnglish.en: Emilio, say hello first and then you order, no rush.
Excuse me, Brenda, could you bring us the allergen binder?
Auntie, don't order anything until we confirm the ingredients.
If the mole is sold out, what do you recommend instead?
Thank you, Brenda, but without seeing the ingredients we won't risk it.
I'm letting you know the allergen binder was missing today.
Hi, I'm writing because we're going to arrive 20 minutes late.
We'd come back as long as the allergen binder is on display.

sourcePassageEnglish: On Sunday, Daniel takes five relatives to have breakfast at the Hotel Azulejo, in Puebla, before visiting Café Cholula.
His nephew Emilio wants to practice Spanish, so Daniel tells him: Emilio, say hello first and then you order, no rush.
Emilio orders the chalupas and a champurrado, and the cook makes them on the griddle next to the counter.
Daniel looks for the allergen binder for his aunt Rosa, who is allergic to peanuts, but it isn't on the table.
Daniel: Excuse me, Brenda, could you bring us the allergen binder?
Brenda looks at the entrance, but she comes back without it because nobody can find it today.
Daniel: Auntie, don't order anything until we confirm the ingredients.
Aunt Rosa wanted the mole poblano, but Brenda explains that it is sold out today.
Daniel: If the mole is sold out, what do you recommend instead?
Brenda offers the pipián as a substitute, but she doesn't know if the sauce contains peanuts.
Daniel: Thank you, Brenda, but without seeing the ingredients we won't risk it.
Brenda asks in the kitchen and confirms that the pipián does contain peanuts, but the enfrijoladas don't.
Emilio: If we hadn't waited, aunt Rosa would have ordered the pipián.
Daniel places the order for the six of them and orders the enfrijoladas for aunt Rosa with a note about her allergy.
The cousins order the potato molotes, and uncle Javier prefers the breaded steak cemitas to go.
After breakfast, Daniel writes to Lupita, the café's host: Hi, I'm writing because we're going to arrive 20 minutes late.
When he hands in the keys, Daniel tells the hotel manager: I'm letting you know the allergen binder was missing today.
The manager asks him to fill out the satisfaction survey, and Daniel writes: We'd come back as long as the allergen binder is on display.

sourceVerbsEnglish.exampleEnglish: Emilio orders the chalupas with no rush.
Brenda confirms the ingredients in the kitchen.

sourceVerbsEnglish.meaningEnglish: to let someone know, to notify
sourceVerbsEnglish.exampleEnglish: I let the manager know before leaving.
We're coming back to the hotel next year.

sourceGrammarExamplesEnglish: You ask Brenda, and if she doesn't know, have her check with the kitchen.
If we hadn't checked the binder, my aunt would have ordered the pipián.

lessons.objectiveFrenchCourseEnglish: Accompagner une commande, vérifier les besoins alimentaires, réorganiser le groupe et faire un suivi factuel.
lessons.focusEnglish: Capstone: polite commands, conditional alternatives, factual reporting, a text update and checkout feedback.
lessons.focusFrench: Bilan : consignes polies, solutions au conditionnel, compte rendu factuel, message et avis au départ.
lessons.teachingNotesEnglish: The allergic guest does not eat café food when ingredients or cross-contact cannot be confirmed. The group uses its own alternative plan.

passage.titleFrench: Gérer un petit-déjeuner de groupe compliqué
english: On Sunday, Daniel brings five relatives to breakfast at a Montréal hotel café.
His nephew Émile wants to order in French, so Daniel encourages him to greet the server first.
Émile asks for the breakfast platter and a hot chocolate.
Daniel’s aunt Rosa has a serious peanut allergy and asks for current ingredient information.
The server, Brenda, looks for the written information but cannot find an updated copy.
Daniel asks how the food is prepared and whether equipment is shared.
Brenda says she cannot confirm those details yet.
Daniel tells Rosa that they will wait before choosing any café food for her.
The breakfast platter is sold out, so Émile asks which other items are listed.
Brenda names a pastry, but she still cannot confirm its ingredients or preparation.
Daniel thanks her and says Rosa will not order café food without clear information.
Rosa uses the alternative breakfast she brought for herself.
The other relatives place their own orders after checking the menu.
Daniel sends the next host a message that the group will be about twenty minutes late.
At checkout, he tells the hotel manager the ingredient information was unavailable.
He does not claim that a particular food caused harm.
The manager asks him to complete a feedback form, and Daniel writes a factual summary.
He says the group would consider returning if clear information and service were improved.
french: Dimanche, Daniel accompagne cinq proches au café d’un hôtel à Montréal pour le petit-déjeuner.
Son neveu Émile veut commander en français ; Daniel l’encourage donc à saluer d’abord la serveuse.
Émile demande l’assiette déjeuner et un chocolat chaud.
La tante de Daniel, Rosa, a une grave allergie aux arachides et demande les renseignements actuels sur les ingrédients.
La serveuse, Brenda, cherche les renseignements écrits, mais ne trouve pas de version à jour.
Daniel demande comment les plats sont préparés et si le matériel est partagé.
Brenda dit qu’elle ne peut pas encore confirmer ces détails.
Daniel dit à Rosa qu’ils attendront avant de choisir un plat du café pour elle.
L’assiette déjeuner est épuisée ; Émile demande donc quels autres plats figurent au menu.
Brenda mentionne une viennoiserie, mais ne peut toujours pas en confirmer les ingrédients ni la préparation.
Daniel la remercie et dit que Rosa ne commandera rien au café sans renseignements clairs.
Rosa utilise le petit-déjeuner de rechange qu’elle a apporté pour elle-même.
Les autres proches passent leurs commandes après avoir consulté le menu.
Daniel envoie un message à leur prochain hôte pour signaler que le groupe aura environ vingt minutes de retard.
Au départ, il dit au responsable de l’hôtel que les renseignements sur les ingrédients étaient indisponibles.
Il n’affirme pas qu’un plat en particulier a causé un problème de santé.
Le responsable lui demande de remplir un formulaire de commentaires ; Daniel rédige un résumé factuel.
Il dit que le groupe envisagerait de revenir si les renseignements et le service étaient améliorés.

verbs.exampleEnglish: The group would consider returning if information improved.
verbs.exampleFrench: Le groupe envisagerait de revenir si les renseignements étaient améliorés.

grammarExamples.english: If we had assumed the pastry was suitable, we might have overlooked the uncertainty.

lessons.speakingInstructionEnglish: Coach Émile’s order, ask about Rosa’s allergy, use the alternative breakfast when details remain unknown, update the next host and give factual checkout feedback.
lessons.speakingFrench: Émile, salue la serveuse avant de commander. Pourriez-vous confirmer les ingrédients et la préparation ? Sans renseignements clairs, Rosa utilisera son autre petit-déjeuner. J’informerai le responsable au départ.
